title: Previewer: reusable blocks with dynamic block identifiers

context.goal: Add support for reusable preview blocks in config/preview.json, with dynamic block name templates like "ehcp_message_ev_cmd_{protocol_type}_block" resolved from parsed variables.
constraints: Keep existing preview configs working (backward compatible).
Do not change EHCP parsing logic semantics except by enabling blocks.
Blocks must work for nested parsing (match/fields) and for SRING->EHCP and direct EHCP formats.

acceptance_criteria: schemas/klogg-previews.schema.json validates configs with top-level "blocks" and fields using format/source "block" + "block" property.
Previewer loads config with "blocks" and can resolve both static and dynamic block references.
Dynamic block reference replaces {var} placeholders with raw parsed values (not enum labels).
Block references can be nested; cycles are detected and reported as preview errors (no crash).
If a block is missing, preview shows a clear error node but does not fail entire preview.
Docs (config/preview.json and/or previews.md) updated with a minimal blocks example.

instructions: Add optional top-level property "blocks": array of block definitions.
Define "block" objects as field-like definitions with required "name".
Allow fields and blocks to reference other blocks via either format:"block" OR source:"block" plus required property "block" (string).
Allow dynamic block names (schema cannot validate placeholders; just accept string).
Keep existing conditional: require "capture" only when source=="capture".
Keep existing validation for match/fields/enum/flags/bitfield maps.
Add in-memory storage for blocks: map<string, FieldDefinitionLike> blocksByName.
Ensure block names are unique; on duplicates log an error and keep the first (or last) deterministically.
Expose blocks map to the runtime parser.
Parse optional top-level "blocks" array before previews.
Each block entry uses the same parsing logic as a field definition (except name is required and used as key).
Keep backward compatibility: configs without blocks must still load.
Implement block invocation for fields where format=="block" OR source=="block".
Add property to FieldDefinition: optional blockTemplate string.
When parsing such a field: resolve block name template by substituting {var} using the current parse context variable table.
Substitution MUST use RAW values captured/extracted (pre-enum label).
Then lookup resolved name in blocks map; if missing, emit an error node under that field and continue parsing safely.
Parse the resolved block as if it were inlined at the current parse point (but keep the invoking field's name in the output tree).
Support blocks that themselves use source:capture, bufferCapture, match, nested fields, etc.
Implement recursion guard / cycle detection: maintain a stack of resolved block names; if a block appears twice in stack, emit error and stop that branch.
Add helper: resolveTemplateString("ehcp_message_command_{command_id}_block", vars) -> string.
Replace all occurrences of {identifier} with vars[identifier] converted to string.
If identifier missing, leave placeholder unchanged and let lookup fail (but include a clear error).
Do not evaluate arithmetic in block templates (only substitution).
Ensure parse context stores both rawValue and displayValue (or at least rawValue) per field name.
Width expressions continue using numeric value where needed (existing behavior).
Block template substitution uses rawValue as string for identifiers like protocol_type, command_id.
Add documentation section: "Reusable blocks"
Explain blocks array, invoking via format:"block" or source:"block" and property "block".
Explain dynamic block names with placeholders {var}.
Include a minimal working example similar to EHCP protocol_type dispatch.
Add a small unit/integration test (where existing preview tests live) that loads a config containing blocks and dynamic block references.
Feed a sample input that sets protocol_type=P and command_id=CM and verify it resolves the correct block and produces expected tree nodes.
Add a test for missing block and for cyclic block reference.

notes: Your provided EHCP blocks config should become valid and runnable after these changes.
No UI changes are strictly required; blocks are transparent to the UI tree.
If desired, later we can add UI hints like showing which block was resolved in a tooltip/debug string.
